title: Same event handler scriptblock variable registered twice on the same object (double-fire)
description: PowerShell WinForms event handler methods (Add_Click, Add_Tick, Add_FormClosing, etc.) accumulate delegates — calling Add_Click($handler) twice on the same object registers the handler twice. This causes the handler body to execute twice per event: duplicate log writes, duplicate navigation, duplicate mutations, duplicate API calls, or race conditions on UI controls. A common occurrence is when the same $handlerName variable is used with Add_<Event> in separate code blocks (e.g. builder block + re-declaration block) due to copy-paste or iterative refactoring. In Start-LocalWebEngineService.ps1 the $exitItemClick handler was added via Add_Click twice on $exitItem.
detection_method: Per-file scan: collect all .Add_<EventName>($varName) calls; flag any ($object, $varName) pair that appears more than once. The regex below detects the simpler form where the same Add_<Event>($var) literal appears twice in the same file.
preventionRule:
Never call Add_<Event> more than once with the same handler variable on the same object. If refreshing handlers, call Remove_<Event> first:
  $btn.Remove_Click($handler)
  $btn.Add_Click($handler)
Or assign via direct event property when available.
remedy: Remove the duplicate Add_<Event> call. If both registrations exist intentionally (different code paths), consolidate into a single registration point and have the handler branch internally.
scan_note: The scan_regex detects the call form; deduplication logic in the scanner must group by (file, varName) and flag count > 1.

known_instances.risk: MEDIUM — causes $timer.Stop() and ExitThread() to run twice on menu exit click
